title: SREV-010 UAC helper wait boundary

wait_api_shape.description: WaitForSingleObject returns WAIT_OBJECT_0, WAIT_TIMEOUT, or WAIT_FAILED; INFINITE means return only on signaled

terminate_warning.description: TerminateProcess does not run normal cleanup and is only safe on processes whose threads are in known states

helper_topology.description: Sandboxie Start.exe uac_prompt helper is a dedicated prompt process launched only for this broker decision and may exit with IDYES or IDNO

bounded_wait.description: WaitForSingleObject(pi.hProcess, SBIE_UAC_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS) replaces INFINITE only for the dedicated uac_prompt helper wait

outcome_routing.description: WAIT_OBJECT_0 reads helper exit code; WAIT_TIMEOUT terminates the dedicated helper and sets ERROR_TIMEOUT; WAIT_FAILED also fails closed; all failure paths reach the existing RunUacSlave3(JustFail=true) path

constant_owner.description: SBIE_UAC_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 is a named constant, not an inline magic number

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate: hung Start.exe uac_prompt does not pin an SbieSvc worker forever; normal IDYES and IDNO prompt exits keep current behavior

contracts: WaitForSingleObject can return WAIT_OBJECT_0, WAIT_TIMEOUT, or WAIT_FAILED
INFINITE wait on a UI helper process pins the broker worker thread
Only the dedicated uac_prompt helper wait is bounded; other Sandboxie WaitForSingleObject calls are out of scope
WAIT_TIMEOUT must terminate the helper and route through JustFail
WAIT_FAILED must route through JustFail without termination side effects beyond the helper
Timeout magnitude is named through SBIE_UAC_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS
